header:
Date: 2025-12-16
Time: 15:30 UTC
Duration: 52 minutes
Attendees: Ava Martinez (Redwood AE), Sandeep Rao (Redwood SE), Maya Thompson (Redwood SE), Diane Park (EmberCloud Head of ML), Roberto Salazar (EmberCloud Security Architect), Lina Chen (EmberCloud Platform), Rajiv Menon (EmberCloud SRE)
Recording link: <redacted>
summary: POC scoping call to define success criteria, workload sizing, and data handling constraints for an EmberCloud POC. Focus areas: PII minimization in prompts, logging/redaction strategies, retention window for prompt/storage, hosted vs dedicated deployment trade-offs, and a 3-phase benchmark plan (latency, throughput, cost). Agreed next steps: Redwood to send POC doc + benchmark harness; EmberCloud to share redacted sample prompts and KMS requirements.
topics:
1) Success criteria and SLOs
2) Data handling: PII redaction, prompt storage, retention windows
3) Workload sizing & traffic patterns
4) Benchmark plan and metrics
5) Deployment options and security controls
6) Timeline and next steps
transcript:
[00:00] Ava Martinez: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. We're gonna run through POC scope — I'll start with goals, then Sandeep will jump into benchmark ideas.
[00:08] Diane Park: Thanks Ava, appreciate it. Quick context: we're EmberCloud, building an AI-assisted config assistant that ingests user infra snippets and... uh, suggests manifests. We're super sensitive about secrets and PII in prompts.
[00:18] Roberto Salazar: Yeah, security is the blocker here. We need assurance that prompts won't be stored in cleartext, and redaction handles things like IPs, creds, and account ids.
[00:27] Sandeep Rao: Understood. For POC we're proposing three workloads — small dev traffic (avg 5 rps), mid-stage (50 rps), and bursty enterprise (200 rps) for short windows. We'll create a harness that replays redacted real prompts to mimic latencies.
[00:38] Lina Chen: Quick question on the 200 rps — what batch sizes and concurrency are you assuming?
[00:44] Sandeep Rao: Good call. We'll test with single-request streaming and with batching up to 8 requests per GPU core. Baseline will be single-stream 95th percentile latency target under 350ms for short contexts, and under 600ms for long contexts (3k tokens).
[00:57] Rajiv Menon: 600ms seems tight for 3k tokens on hosted. Do you have numbers for dedicated capacity?
[00:62] Sandeep Rao: Dedicated will be better — we expect 95p around 300-400ms for long contexts when using our dedicted pools and KV cache optimizations. There's some transcription hiccup there: means 'dedicated' pools and KV cache.
[01:12] Diane Park: On PII: our initial requirement is no raw prompt logs kept beyond a rolling 24-hour window, and any persisted prompt data must be tokenized/anonymized. We may need zero retention for some enterprise customers.
[01:22] Ava Martinez: We support configurable retention windows. For POC we can run two variants: 24-hour rolling, and ephemeral (no storage except in-memory during request). We also have a token-level redaction feature proposition — run a regex/NER pass before persist.
[01:32] Roberto Salazar: Regex won't catch everything. We need deterministic redaction rules, plus an option to not store prompts at all. Also KMS for keys and audit logs.
[01:40] Maya Thompson: Noted. For deterministic redaction we recommend a two-stage approach: client-side redaction libraries (customer-run) + server-side NER as a fallback. For the POC we can show both: customer-supplied redaction + Redwood's server-side approximate redaction.
[01:52] Diane Park: That helps. What's the plan for prompt storage when we need to run evals?
[02:00] Sandeep Rao: We'll propose keeping only hashed prompt fingerprints + metadata (no full prompt) for eval traceability. If EmberCloud requires full prompt for quality checks, we can store it encrypted with customer KMS and ensure access controls and TTLs.
[02:10] Diane Park: Hashing alone may not be enough for debugging. We'll likely ask for an encrypted archive accessible only during a short window. Can you do HSM-backed KMS?
[02:20] Ava Martinez: Yes — Redwood Private and Dedicated both integrate with customer KMS/HSM in most major providers; for hosted we can also support customer-managed keys in some regions. We'll document exact flows in the security pack.
[02:30] Rita (mislabelled as speaker): uh, sorry, that's me, Roberto interjection — what about redaction accuracy? If your NER wrongly redacts domain names that we need, that breaks our assistant.
[02:40] Sandeep Rao: Good point. We'll capture false-positive/negative rates in the benchmark by including golden annotations in the sample dataset. That will be part of the POC success criteria: redaction precision >= 95% for PII entities, recall >= 90% (numbers adjustable).
[02:52] Diane Park: Okay, success criteria — let's list them: 1) latency SLOs for our mid and peak workloads, 2) redaction accuracy thresholds, 3) storage/retention policy compliance, 4) secure key management and audit logs, and 5) cost estimate under expected volume.
[03:08] Ava Martinez: I'll capture that. For benchmarking, we propose a 2-week harness: Week 1 small and mid workloads with synthetic replay; Week 2 peak/burst tests and redaction accuracy tests.
[03:20] Rajiv Menon: Do you simulate cold starts and model fallbacks? We have concerns about regional outages.
[03:27] Sandeep Rao: Yes, we'll include fallback tests — model variant fallback and cross-region failover. Also simulate autoscale to observe tail latencies.
[03:34] Lina Chen: Regarding telemetry, what will you log in the hosted option? We need per-token costs and token-level breakdowns but without storing content.
[03:42] Maya Thompson: We capture token counts, model variant, route latency, and aggregated histograms. Content is only stored when retention is enabled; otherwise we keep fingerprints and aggregated stats.
[03:50] Roberto Salazar: One more ask: we need redaction rules to be auditable. Can you surface the NER decisions (flags) without exposing the raw tokens?
[03:58] Sandeep Rao: We can store redaction diffs as masked templates and flags — e.g., "[REDACTED_EMAIL] user@..." — but yes that needs to avoid exposure. We'll provide formats in the POC doc.
[04:08] Diane Park: Timelines — EmberCloud wants to start in January, full 4-week pilot then expand if metrics pass. Can you commit to delivering the harness and security pack before then?
[04:17] Ava Martinez: We can deliver the POC doc + harness skeleton by 2025-12-20 and the security pack by 2025-12-23. Pilot kick-off the week of Jan 5th works from our side.
[04:25] Rajiv Menon: What about cost modeling — we need an estimate for the pilot and an extrapolation to peak.
[04:30] Sandeep Rao: We'll provide a per-token and per-hourized GPU cost estimate for hosted vs dedicated. For the pilot we'll include a sample billing forecast for 50 rps sustained over 4 weeks and an upper-bound peak simulation.
[04:40] Lina Chen: For the POC, can you support our internal SSO? We use SAML with SCIM for provisioning.
[04:45] Ava Martinez: Yes, we'll add SAML + SCIM integration to the security pack and help with onboarding.
[04:50] Diane Park: Anything else?
[04:53] Roberto Salazar: Procurement may need a data processing agreement and SOC2 attestation copies.
[04:58] Ava Martinez: We'll attach SOC 2 summary and the DPA template; legal can chat after the POC scope doc.
[05:04] Diane Park: Great. Quick recap?
[05:06] Ava Martinez: Recap: Redwood to send POC doc, benchmark harness, security pack (incl. KMS flows, SAML/SCIM notes) by dates we listed. EmberCloud provides redacted prompts, golden annotations for redaction tests, and any additional compliance requirements. Pilot kicks off week of Jan 5th.
[05:18] Diane Park: Perfect. Thanks everyone.
[05:20] Ava Martinez: Thanks all, we'll follow up with calendar invites and the doc.
[05:24] (call ends)
notes: Transcript has occasional mislabels and minor ASR errors (e.g., 'dedicated' transcribed as 'dedicted' earlier). Customers emphasized PII minimization and KMS/HSM requirements. Agreed benchmark plan: 2-week harness + 2-week pilot window; success criteria capture latency, redaction accuracy, retention compliance, and cost.
